findings.reason: a build node reading the decision log finds two live, mutually exclusive answers on whether a caller may name a lane, and §1's line 43 ("The orchestrator does not pick") inherits the superseded one, so the plan's own authority model is undecided.
findings.text: decision `selection-authority` (data-choice `router-decides-orchestrator-comments`, "resolved" 2026-10-02) states the orchestrator influences the pick "never by naming a lane", while decision `local-is-authoritative` (2026-10-06, line 137) states "An explicit --local (or --backend) is authoritative" and `picker-chooses-the-lane` (2026-10-07, line 141) says "A named lane stays authoritative"; both decisions are recorded as decided and neither marks the earlier one superseded

findings.reason: the plan's own §1 asserts a relationship the wiring omits, so the DAG a coordinator reads shows no edge to a plan the text says this one absorbs, and `plan-informs` on the same target as `plan-after` states the ordering in both directions.
findings.text: the header declares `plan-after="the-local-lane-is-the-default"` and `plan-informs="a-window-paces-the-lane,the-local-lane-is-the-default"` but no relationship to `advise-the-lane-never-force-it`, which §1 (line 44) names as one of the three plans this one "is meant to absorb the routing parts of"

findings.reason: the two gates are closed/passed and their `required_evidence` still names the anchor, so a reader loses a convenience link rather than a claim; the same prose-in-href pattern appears in other plans, so this is cosmetic and conventional rather than a mis-citation.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — the two `r-gate-evidence` anchors carry whole evidence sentences as their href value rather than a path, so the surface renders them as links that resolve to nothing; every intra-plan href (`s2`, `s6-fallout`, `s6-jev-chooses-the-lane`) and every cited evidence fragment otherwise resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each section states a measurable done-when with a falsifiable control: §6's week comparison publishes success rate, metered spend, fallback rate and confidence against deterministic routing, and the reversal condition (success no lower, spend no higher, zero refused-model dispatches) is a target that can fail and reverse the switch.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate evidence and every fragment cited sit under docs/evidence/fragments/one-typesafe-model-picker/ or docs/evidence/archive/, and the followups point at durable report directories, not session scratchpads.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag is required in any symbol or comment the plan prescribes; the `f-otmp-*` and `s6-*` identifiers appear only as plan data (followup and anchor ids), which is where they belong.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the Decisions section records two answers that contradict each other on whether a coordinator may name a lane, and §1's authority sentence carries the superseded side.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable (§2 disposition of codex-spark, §4 the Jev design note, §11 the catalogue move, and so on).
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — §1 states the plan overlaps `advise-the-lane-never-force-it` and "is meant to absorb the routing parts of all three", but the header declares no relationship to that plan (which exists at docs/plans/advise-the-lane-never-force-it.html), and `plan-informs` lists `the-local-lane-is-the-default`, the same plan the header already names in `plan-after`.
